summary: Hiding navigation with Ctrl+B and showing it again leaves History's column boundaries exactly where they were: History keeps its measured width exactly, so the same window width lays the columns out the same way
limitations: Linux X11 under XWayland with Mutter input. This scenario runs at scale factor 1, where every layout width is a whole pixel; a scenario cannot set the scale factor, so the frames at 1.25 were taken with qa.py launch --scale 1.25 at 2003 x 1000 (logical 1602.4 x 800, where History is 1271 device px wide at 13 pt and 1179 at 18 pt, 1016.8 and 943.2 logical), outside the scenario, and qa.py recheck does not re-check them. On X11 the base's frames before and after Ctrl+B twice are identical too, so the shift the change removes is carried by the GPUI view test history_columns_return_after_toggling_navigation (1398 px at scale factor 1.25), not by these frames. The window is 1600 x 800, wider than History's house size, because at 1480 x 800 the 18 pt inspector leaves History narrower than its columns and Commit message takes no leftover. On both builds the first frame after Ctrl+B hides navigation keeps the header and the list's frame at the earlier width while the rows use the new one, and X11 does not redraw it; it is committed as context. Escape is pressed before the first capture only to enter keyboard mode, so both compared frames draw the list's focus ring. The scope toolbar's switch to its labelled row 1 px of window width sooner does not arise at this width: both builds draw the labelled toolbar. Native Wayland, macOS and a dragged navigation width are not covered
